A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable and describe the same HAT-4D work. Their main papers align closely. V1 includes supplementary Sections 7–14, whereas v2 ends after the references; this omission is a document difference, not an extraction failure.

before.justification: V1 reports original MVOIK-4D benchmark experiments, component and human-intervention ablations, finetuning results, challenging-subset evaluations, and human validation of interaction metrics.

after.justification: V2 retains the original benchmark results and ablations in Tables 1–2 and the finetuning results in Figure 6, despite omitting the supplementary results.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.3 retain the same IKG formulation, generation and composition pipeline, memory-guided propagation, rollback, and human refinement operators. Omission of detailed appendix specifications does not establish a change to the underlying algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions retain MVOIK-4D, including ToolOIK-4D and MemoryOIK-4D, with the same reported 112 scenes and 77 tasks. The omitted challenge analyses partition this existing coverage; they do not introduce a separate dataset or task.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains L4GM, GVFDiffusion, SV4D, STAG4D, and FB4D. The omitted supplementary evaluations reuse these methods; no comparator is added, replaced, or removed within a retained comparison.

E3.justification: V2 omits Section 9.1's separately reported evaluation without human refinement, stratified into depth ambiguity, topology change, and heavy occlusions with 60, 32, and 57 samples. The retained experiments' metrics, intervention budgets, and finetuning split remain unchanged; there is no evidence of rerunning them under revised settings.

E4.justification: V2 loses the challenging-subset analysis, the memory-metric diagnostic case study, quantitative validation against human judgments, and additional qualitative comparisons from Sections 9, 11, and 12. These substantially reduce robustness and metric-validation evidence. Main-paper component, intervention, and view-scaling analyses remain.

E5.justification: V1 Section 11.2 documents Spearman rank-correlation estimation against independent rankings from two human evaluators. V2 retains a general human-consistency claim but omits this statistical procedure and its reporting. Neither version reports seed-based uncertainty or confidence intervals.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and Figure 6 retain their results, but substantial supplementary results disappear. Examples include Table 4's LPIPS scores of 0.1388, 0.1113, and 0.1699 for the three challenging subsets, and Table 5's human-metric correlations of 0.75 for interaction and 0.65 for deformation. Additional qualitative and dataset-distribution results are also omitted.

T1.justification: V2 substantially reduces the mathematical specification by omitting the depth-constrained ROI definition, regularized pose and regional refinement objectives in Section 7.2, and formal memory-metric definitions in Sections 10.2–10.3. These include substantive selection and matching conditions beyond standard metric formulas. The main IKG definition remains unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about the agentic human-assisted framework, IKG, MVOIK-4D benchmark, reconstruction performance, and usefulness for finetuning. Removal of supporting appendix evidence does not alter these stated core claims.

C2.justification: Appendix explanations of why symbolic scene relations improve robustness under occlusion and why semantic memory matching tolerates pixel misalignment disappear. The main interpretations and limitations concerning flexible deformation, fast non-rigid motion, and VLM dependence remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 omits extensive reproducibility information: frame sampling, editor and optimization instructions, the SV4D 2.0 refinement specification, metric preprocessing and the 0.75 matching threshold, human-evaluation details, and full agent/evaluator prompts in Sections 13–14. Main settings and the project link remain, but do not replace these disclosures.

R1.justification: Four works cited in the supplement disappear from the bibliography: CLIP, FVD, SV4D 2.0, and LPIPS. The main related-work discussion and research positioning otherwise remain unchanged; the other citation differences are renumbering.

P1.justification: The entire explanatory supplement, Sections 7–14, is removed, substantially contracting the document's structure and exposition while leaving main-paper prose intact. Main-text references to appendix details remain unresolved. A smaller edit adds a second affiliation for Mingyu Zhang.

P2.justification: V2 omits Figures 8–16 and Tables 3–5, including editor screenshots, dataset distributions, metric diagnostics, subset comparisons, and additional reconstruction examples. Main Figures 1–7 and Tables 1–2 retain their displays; the principal visual change is removal of the supplementary presentation.

improvement.justification: V2 preserves the principal claims and main results while removing important evidence for challenging-case performance and metric validity, together with detailed optimization specifications and agent prompts needed for reproduction. Main-text promises of appendix support remain unfulfilled. These losses substantially weaken substantiation and reproducibility, with no compensating scientific improvement in the supplied PDF.
